key_points: Gradio's gr.Workflow tool allows users to create AI pipelines as graphs of nodes with a drag-and-drop interface.
The same graph functions as a REST API and can be deployed to Hugging Face Spaces with one command.
Each workflow output has its own REST endpoint, enabling direct code calls without UI interaction.
The tool supports local GPU usage via the @spaces.GPU decorator, reducing reliance on external inference providers.
Gradio's workflow enables parallel processing through fan-out patterns, making it versatile for various AI applications.
items.summary: Gradio introduces gr.Workflow, a tool that allows users to create AI pipelines as graphs of nodes. The interface provides a drag-and-drop canvas where each node is runnable and intermediate results are visible. The same graph functions as a REST API and can be deployed to Hugging Face Spaces with one command. The tool supports multiple workflows, such as image editing, text-to-speech, and dataset analysis, with each output having its own REST endpoint. Users can call these endpoints directly from code without opening the UI. The workflow can also utilize local GPUs via the @spaces.GPU decorator, allowing models to run without relying on external inference providers. The tool simplifies the creation of APIs and enables parallel processing through fan-out patterns, making it versatile for various AI applications.
items.title: Gradio's Workflow Tool Enables AI Pipelines with Drag-and-Drop Interface

key_points: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers up to 30x higher throughput per megawatt than GB300 NVL72 for agentic AI workloads.
Agentic AI tasks require significantly more tokens than simple chat requests due to their complex, multi-step nature.
The Vera Rubin platform reduces token cost by up to 35x, enabling continuous, large-scale agent operation.
NVIDIA attributes performance gains to extreme codesign across hardware and software, including disaggregated serving and NVFP4 quantization.
The platform's scale-up domain, supported by NVLink interconnects, enables efficient inter-GPU communication and large-scale inference optimizations.
items.summary: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 system demonstrates up to 30x higher throughput per megawatt than its GB300 NVL72 counterpart for agentic AI workloads, according to NVIDIA. The performance was measured using the SemiAnalysis AgentX workload, which simulates real-world agentic coding sessions with context growth and sub-agent interactions. Agentic AI tasks, such as investment research or software development, require significantly more tokens than simple chat requests due to their complex, multi-step nature. The Vera Rubin platform also reduces token cost by up to 35x, enabling continuous, large-scale agent operation. NVIDIA attributes these gains to extreme codesign across hardware and software, including disaggregated serving, rate matching, and NVFP4 quantization. The platform's scale-up domain, supported by NVLink interconnects, enables efficient inter-GPU communication and large-scale inference optimizations.
items.title: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin NVL72 Achieves 30x Higher Efficiency for Agentic AI Workloads

key_points: NVIDIA's Vera CPU is designed to balance single-thread performance and concurrency for agentic AI workloads.
Telemetry from 163,594 sessions shows agentic tasks have highly variable trajectories with long sequential chains and sporadic parallel bursts.
Traditional CPU designs struggle to accommodate this variability, either sacrificing latency or failing to handle parallel demands.
The Vera CPU's Olympus cores maintain strong per-thread performance while providing sufficient concurrency for parallel workloads.
NVIDIA claims the Vera CPU delivers up to 1.5x agentic performance compared to competitors, improving fleet economics.
items.summary: NVIDIA's Vera CPU is designed to address the challenges of agentic AI workloads by balancing single-thread performance and concurrency. Based on telemetry from 163,594 sessions, agentic tasks exhibit highly variable trajectories with long sequential chains and sporadic parallel bursts. Traditional CPU designs struggle to accommodate this variability, as they either prioritize core count at the expense of latency or fail to handle transient fan-out demands. The Vera CPU, with its Olympus cores, maintains strong per-thread performance while providing sufficient concurrency to manage parallel workloads. This design reduces latency on the critical sequential path and absorbs intermittent bursts of parallel computation. NVIDIA claims the Vera CPU delivers up to 1.5x agentic performance compared to competitors, improving fleet economics by maximizing completed user sessions. The architecture also minimizes memory and power overhead, ensuring efficient resource utilization across the entire workload trajectory.
items.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU Optimizes Agentic AI Workloads with Balanced Performance

key_points: NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX is now in full production, enhancing AI inference performance for agentic systems.
The system achieves 3,400 output tokens per second in benchmarking, setting a new record for the Gemma 4 31B model.
Nebius is the first AI cloud to adopt Groq 3 LPX, integrating it into its Token Factory platform for faster token generation.
Groq 3 LPX addresses the challenges of processing large context and low-latency token generation, improving agentic AI responsiveness.
The platform is optimized with NVIDIA BlueField®-4 DPUs and other components for high throughput and low latency in multi-agent systems.
items.summary: NVIDIA announced that its Groq 3 LPX, an interactive AI inference accelerator, is now in full production. The system extends the performance of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 by significantly increasing token generation rates, enabling faster responses for agentic AI applications. In benchmarking, Groq 3 LPX achieved 3,400 output tokens per second with a 100,000-token context, setting a new record for the Gemma 4 31B model. Nebius, the first AI cloud to adopt the technology, plans to integrate it into its Token Factory platform, offering developers extreme token generation speed. NVIDIA emphasized that Groq 3 LPX addresses the challenges of processing large context and low-latency token generation, enhancing the responsiveness of agentic systems. The platform combines seven chips and five racks, optimized with NVIDIA BlueField®-4 DPUs and other components for high throughput and low latency in multi-agent systems.
items.title: NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX Boosts AI Inference Speed for Agentic Systems

These deepfakes are causing global disruption, confusing police and lawmakers.
The investigation raises concerns about the future of distinguishing fact from fiction with AI.

items.summary: The Guardian's Michael Safi has spent six months investigating an AI company producing deepfakes that are disrupting global efforts by law enforcement and lawmakers. The investigation highlights the challenges of distinguishing fact from fiction in an AI-driven world. Safi's pursuit has raised broader questions about the future of truth in the age of deepfakes. key_points: Situational Awareness, an AI-focused hedge fund, is under SEC investigation after a market downturn.
The SEC has subpoenaed banks that handled the fund's transactions and trading activities.
No wrongdoing has been alleged against the fund, though it is being scrutinized.
The company has not commented but stated it will cooperate with regulatory requests.
items.summary: Situational Awareness, an AI-focused hedge fund led by Leopold Aschenbrenner, is under SEC scrutiny following a significant market downturn. The fund, which experienced rapid growth before losing billions in value, is being investigated as the SEC subpoenas banks that handled its transactions. key_points: A Stanford study shows a 19 percent decline in entry-level jobs for young workers in AI-exposed fields.
The research uses ADP payroll data and AI exposure metrics to track employment trends.
Younger workers face greater AI-driven job losses compared to older workers.
The study updates previous findings, showing a widening gap in employment levels.
The Anthropic Economic Index and labor market impact gauge are used to assess AI exposure.
items.summary: A Stanford University study updates its findings on AI's impact on employment, showing a 19 percent drop in entry-level jobs for workers aged 22 to 25 in AI-exposed occupations, compared to a 13 percent gap last year. The research uses ADP payroll data and AI exposure metrics, including the Anthropic Economic Index, to track employment trends. The study highlights that while AI is affecting younger workers, older workers remain largely unaffected. The findings are part of a broader analysis of AI's labor market effects.
items.title: Stanford study shows AI-driven job losses for young workers

key_points: A Deloitte survey highlights that only 15% of organizations have achieved scaled, orchestrated multi-agent deployments.
Most companies struggle to develop an integrated roadmap for agentic AI, with 42% testing small agent numbers and 43% expanding deployments.
Key challenges include a lack of unified data, trust and governance issues, and integration complexity.
Only 1 in 5 businesses said their workforce is ready for agentic AI, with reskilling and upskilling cited as major obstacles.
The research emphasizes that scaling agentic AI requires process redesign, workforce transformation, and rethinking business models.
items.summary: A Deloitte survey of 501 senior business leaders reveals that only 15% of organizations have achieved scaled, orchestrated multi-agent deployments. Most companies struggle to develop an integrated roadmap for agentic AI, with 42% testing small agent numbers and 43% expanding deployments. Key challenges include a lack of unified data (72%), trust and governance issues (70%), and integration complexity (67%). Only 1 in 5 businesses said their workforce is ready for agentic AI, with reskilling and upskilling cited as major obstacles. The research emphasizes that scaling agentic AI requires process redesign, workforce transformation, and rethinking business models, with 74% of leaders expecting significant process changes by 2030.
items.title: Businesses face challenges in scaling agentic AI adoption

key_points: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge is a 4B omni-model optimized for real-time on-device robot control, running on NVIDIA Jetson Thor.
The model is pretrained on physical-world data and post-trained to generate action policies for robotic tasks.
Cosmos 3 Edge achieves 22.9% success in RoboLab tasks, with lower inference compute than larger variants like Cosmos 3 Nano.
Developers can use the open cosmos-framework repo to reproduce results, including dataset preparation and checkpoint conversion.
The policy runs natively on Jetson Thor, eliminating the need for data-center GPUs and enabling continuous action generation.
items.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Cosmos 3 Edge, a 4B omni-model designed for real-time on-device robot control. The model, part of the Cosmos 3 family, is pretrained on physical-world data and optimized to run on NVIDIA Jetson Thor, addressing memory and latency constraints for robotic applications. It enables post-training to generate action policies that operate in closed-loop simulation, achieving 22.9% success in RoboLab tasks. The model is trained on the Cosmos3-DROID dataset, which includes 76k teleoperated trajectories across 86 tasks. Developers can use the open cosmos-framework repo to reproduce the results, with instructions for dataset preparation, checkpoint conversion, and post-training. The policy runs natively on Jetson Thor, eliminating the need for data-center GPUs, and supports continuous action generation through a WebSocket server using the OpenPI protocol. The model's success rate is competitive with larger variants like Cosmos 3 Nano, offering real-time autonomy for physical AI applications.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Cosmos 3 Edge for Real-Time On-Device Robot Control

The model includes a 2B ViT-style encoder for vision and a 28B parameter text decoder.

The model is supported by multiple libraries including transformers, llama.cpp, and vLLM.
Muse Glimmer can handle images, videos, and text, and supports multimodal tool calling.

key_points: MIT researchers are among 15 projects selected for DOE's Genesis Mission Phase I funding.
The initiative seeks to build a science discovery platform using AI, supercomputing, and quantum systems.
Six MIT-led projects focus on quantum sensing, rare earth element extraction, and fusion reactor modeling.
MIT researchers are also involved in nine other projects led by external institutions and labs.
Phase I aims to demonstrate AI-integrated research workflows and evaluate scientific merit before potential further funding.
items.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has selected 15 collaborative projects involving MIT researchers for funding under the Genesis Mission Phase I. The initiative aims to create a powerful science discovery platform by integrating AI, supercomputing, and quantum systems to advance energy and national security research. MIT's involvement includes six projects led by its faculty, focusing on quantum sensing, rare earth element extraction, and fusion reactor modeling. Additional projects involve partnerships with industry and national labs, with MIT researchers contributing to nine other initiatives. The DOE emphasized the importance of cross-sector collaboration in accelerating scientific discovery through AI integration. Funding for these projects is pending final negotiations, with Phase I focusing on demonstrating research workflows and evaluating scientific merit.
items.title: MIT researchers selected for DOE's Genesis Mission Phase I funding

key_points: Professor Dimitri Bertsekas, a leading computer scientist, died at 83.
Bertsekas contributed to optimization, control, and artificial intelligence, with over 20 influential books.
His work on dynamic programming and stochastic control shaped modern reinforcement learning.
Bertsekas was celebrated for his clear writing and mentorship, influencing generations of researchers.
He received numerous awards, including the INFORMS John von Neumann Theory Prize.
items.summary: Professor Dimitri Bertsekas, a renowned computer scientist and prolific author, died at 83. A Jerry McAfee Emeritus Professor at MIT and Arizona State University, Bertsekas made significant contributions to fields like optimization, control, and artificial intelligence. He authored over 20 influential books and mentored numerous students who became leading researchers. His work on dynamic programming and stochastic control, including co-authored texts, shaped modern reinforcement learning. Bertsekas was known for his clear writing, mentorship, and artistic contributions to his textbooks. He received numerous awards, including the INFORMS John von Neumann Theory Prize. Former students and colleagues remember him as a humble, inspiring figure who deeply impacted academia and education.
items.title: Professor Dimitri Bertsekas, influential computer scientist, dies at 83

key_points: IBM Research proposes an abstraction layer for cryptography to simplify security operations and reduce technical debt.
Current cryptographic practices embed algorithm choices in application code, leading to fragile systems and operational complexity.
The proposed intent-based API separates cryptographic policy from implementation, allowing centralized management of security decisions.
The initiative includes a partial reference implementation and an API specification, inviting community testing and refinement.
The approach is positioned as a necessary evolution for handling post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and future cryptographic changes without code modifications.
items.summary: IBM Research introduces a new approach to cryptographic agility by proposing an abstraction layer that separates cryptographic decisions from application code. Developers currently manage complex security operations manually, embedding algorithm choices directly into code, which leads to fragile systems and technical debt. The proposed solution, inspired by filesystems and networking abstractions, aims to centralize cryptographic policy and allow runtime enforcement of security decisions. The initiative includes an intent-based API that defines cryptographic scopes, enabling interchangeable algorithms within defined categories. This shift would transform cryptography from a development concern to an operational one, managed by security teams. IBM has released an API specification and a partial reference implementation, inviting the community to test and refine the approach. The work is framed as a necessary evolution in response to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption, which requires significant system rearchitecture. The goal is to create a sustainable framework that reduces developer burden and enables future cryptographic changes without code modifications.
items.title: IBM Research proposes cryptographic abstraction layer to simplify security operations

key_points: IBM released CodeAlchemy, a synthetic code dataset with nearly 1 trillion tokens, designed to improve AI models' understanding of code behavior.
The dataset pairs code files with execution traces, offering insights into how code functions during runtime, unlike static code datasets.
CodeAlchemy surpasses existing datasets in scale and scope, covering 15 programming languages and including sandboxed environments for testing.
Initial tests show that training models on CodeAlchemy improves performance, particularly for smaller models, suggesting synthetic data can be more effective than real-world data in some cases.
IBM plans to expand the synthetic data pipeline to other enterprise tasks through Open Alchemy, enabling AI agents to better interact with real-world systems.
items.summary: IBM researchers have released CodeAlchemy, a synthetic code dataset covering 15 programming languages and containing nearly 1 trillion tokens. This dataset aims to enhance AI models' ability to understand code behavior by pairing code files with their execution traces. Unlike previous datasets, CodeAlchemy includes execution traces, helping models grasp how code functions in real scenarios. The dataset surpasses existing code datasets in scale and scope, featuring sandboxed environments for safely testing AI-generated code. Initial tests show improvements in model performance, particularly for smaller models, suggesting synthetic data can be more effective than real-world data in certain cases. IBM plans to expand the synthetic data pipeline to other enterprise tasks through Open Alchemy, enabling AI agents to better interact with real-world systems.
items.title: IBM Releases CodeAlchemy Dataset to Improve AI Code Understanding

key_points: Google has launched Nano Banana 2 Lite, a faster and more cost-efficient image model, and Gemini Omni Flash, a video generation and editing model, for developers.
Nano Banana 2 Lite offers text-to-image outputs in 4 seconds at $0.034 per 1K image, while Gemini Omni Flash is priced at $0.10 per second for video output.
Both models are available in Google AI Studio, Gemini API, and consumer products, with demo apps illustrating their combined use in creative workflows.
The models use SynthID watermarking for content verification, allowing users to check AI-generated content through the Gemini app or Search.
Developers can chain the models for end-to-end multimedia experiences, using Nano Banana 2 Lite for image generation and Gemini Omni Flash for video animation.
items.summary: Google has released Nano Banana 2 Lite, a faster and more cost-efficient image model, and Gemini Omni Flash, a video generation and editing model, for developers. Nano Banana 2 Lite is available in Google AI Studio, Gemini API, and consumer products, offering quick text-to-image outputs in 4 seconds at $0.034 per 1K image. Gemini Omni Flash supports high-quality video creation and conversational editing, priced at $0.10 per second, and is accessible via the same platforms. Both models are designed for creative workflows, with Nano Banana 2 Lite recommended for rapid ideation and Gemini Omni Flash for video editing. Developers can use the models together for end-to-end multimedia experiences, with demo apps showcasing their capabilities. The models use SynthID watermarking for content verification.
items.title: Google Launches Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash for Generative Media

key_points: Google Research introduces TabFM, a foundation model for tabular data that simplifies classification and regression through zero-shot learning.
TabFM eliminates the need for manual hyperparameter tuning and feature engineering by using in-context learning with synthetic datasets.
The model is trained on hundreds of millions of synthetic datasets generated via structural causal models to capture complex feature relationships.
TabFM outperforms traditional supervised algorithms in benchmarks and is integrated into Google BigQuery for easy use.
The hybrid architecture of TabFM combines elements from TabPFN and TabICL to handle the two-dimensional nature of tabular data.
items.summary: Google Research introduces TabFM, a foundation model for tabular data that simplifies classification and regression tasks through zero-shot learning. Traditional methods like XGBoost require extensive manual effort, but TabFM uses in-context learning to eliminate the need for hyperparameter tuning and feature engineering. The model is trained on synthetic datasets generated via structural causal models, enabling it to generalize well to real-world data. TabFM outperforms existing supervised algorithms in benchmarks and is integrated into Google BigQuery for easy use. The model's hybrid architecture combines elements from TabPFN and TabICL, allowing it to handle the two-dimensional nature of tabular data.
items.title: Google Introduces TabFM for Zero-Shot Tabular Data Prediction

key_points: Google introduces Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to retrofit existing Gemini Nano v3 models for improved on-device AI efficiency.
MTP reduces memory usage and processing time by integrating a lightweight transformer head into the main model's architecture.
The technique enables faster AI features like notification summaries and text proofreading without compromising model accuracy.
Experiments show up to 50% speed improvements on Pixel 9 devices, with significant memory savings compared to standalone drafters.
Google is exploring further optimizations, including parallel decoding and verification leniency, to enhance performance under mobile constraints.
items.summary: Google researchers introduce a method to retrofit Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) onto existing Gemini Nano v3 models, improving on-device inference efficiency. This approach addresses the limitations of autoregressive text generation on mobile devices, which are constrained by energy and memory limits. By integrating a lightweight MTP head into the model's final layers, Google reduces memory usage and processing time, enabling faster AI features like notification summaries and text proofreading. The MTP head leverages the main model's internal state to predict future tokens, eliminating the need for separate, memory-heavy drafters. This retrofitting technique maintains the original model's accuracy and safety while achieving up to 50% speed improvements on Pixel 9 devices. Google also highlights further optimizations, including parallel decoding and verification leniency, to enhance performance under mobile constraints.
items.title: Google Enhances On-Device AI Efficiency with Multi-Token Prediction on Pixel Phones

Domyn's Domyn Small model leverages Ai2's Dolma and Dolci datasets for full auditability and traceability.
AISquared's Bolt models are fine-tuned from Olmo, benefiting from its transparency and permissive licensing.
Both companies highlight Ai2's openness as critical for meeting legal and security requirements.
Ai2's approach supports compliance with regulations like the EU AI Act and U.S. federal constraints.
items.summary: Two AI labs, Domyn and AISquared, have developed models based on Ai2's open releases to meet compliance needs in regulated sectors. Domyn's Domyn Small model uses Ai2's Dolma and Dolci datasets, enabling full auditability and traceability. AISquared's Bolt models are fine-tuned from Olmo, benefiting from its transparency and permissive licensing. The article emphasizes how Ai2's approach supports compliance with regulations like the EU AI Act and U.S. federal constraints.
items.title: Domyn and AISquared leverage Ai2's open models for regulated industry compliance

key_points: MolmoMotion forecasts 3D motion of objects using video, language instructions, and query points, outperforming existing methods.
The model is trained on MolmoMotion-1M, the largest dataset of action-described 3D point trajectories, and evaluated on PointMotionBench.
Two variants of the model—autoregressive and flow-matching—handle different forecasting scenarios, improving accuracy and uncertainty representation.
MolmoMotion enhances robotics planning and video generation, achieving better task success and motion quality compared to baseline models.
The researchers highlight forecasting motion as a key component of machine intelligence, with future work aimed at improving handling of complex deformable motion.
items.summary: Researchers introduce MolmoMotion, a new model that forecasts 3D motion of objects based on video input, language instructions, and query points. The model outperforms existing methods in predicting future trajectories of objects like bowls, cars, and flamingos. MolmoMotion-1M, a large dataset of 3D point trajectories paired with action descriptions, and PointMotionBench, a benchmark for evaluating motion forecasting accuracy, are also released. The model uses two variants—autoregressive and flow-matching—to handle different forecasting scenarios. It shows promise in robotics planning and video generation, improving task success rates and motion quality. The researchers emphasize the importance of forecasting motion as a fundamental aspect of machine intelligence, with plans to expand the model's capabilities in the future.
items.title: MolmoMotion predicts 3D object motion from language and video

key_points: Amazon has launched Graviton5 processors, powering new M9g and M9gd EC2 instances, marking the fifth generation of its custom silicon.
Graviton5 doubles the core count from 96 to 192 and supports DDR5-8800 memory and PCIe gen6 interconnects.
The three-nanometer process enables greater circuit density and faster on-chip communication, with each core offering 25% better performance.
The Neoverse V3 core improves branch prediction, enhancing database performance by up to 30%.
Graviton5 features a restructured chiplet architecture with four chiplets, each containing 48 cores, DRAM controllers, and PCIe controllers, providing 420 gigabytes per second of bandwidth.
items.summary: Amazon has released the Graviton5 processors, powering new M9g and M9gd EC2 instances, marking the fifth generation of its custom silicon. Graviton5 doubles the core count from 96 to 192 and supports DDR5-8800 memory and PCIe gen6 interconnects. The three-nanometer process enables greater circuit density and faster on-chip communication, with each core offering 25% better performance. The Neoverse V3 core improves branch prediction, enhancing database performance by up to 30%. Graviton5 features a restructured chiplet architecture with four chiplets, each containing 48 cores, DRAM controllers, and PCIe controllers, providing 420 gigabytes per second of bandwidth. This design allows for more efficient memory latency management and NUMA region configuration. The Nitro Isolation Engine, a formally verified component, enhances security by enforcing VM isolation through mathematical precision.
items.title: Amazon Launches Graviton5 Processors with Enhanced Performance and Security

key_points: NIST has expanded its mass spectral library to include over 382,180 chemical fingerprints.
The updated NIST26 library assists in identifying unknown substances through mass spectrometry.
The Electron Ionization (EI) component now includes 35,000 new compounds, while the Tandem Library has 17,000 new entries.
NIST scientists use a software-based evaluation process to maintain the library's standards.
items.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has expanded its mass spectral library, known as Standard Reference Database 1A, to include hundreds of thousands of chemical fingerprints. This update, called NIST26, aids researchers and manufacturers in identifying unknown substances through mass spectrometry. The library contains 382,180 entries in the Electron Ionization (EI) component and 68,635 in the Tandem Library. NIST scientists use a software-based evaluation process to ensure accuracy. The updated database is available for purchase and is preinstalled on many commercial mass spectrometers.
items.title: NIST Updates Chemical Fingerprint Library to Identify Unknown Substances

key_points: Apostol Vassilev's proof shows no finite guardrails can fully protect AI from adversarial prompts.
The research builds on Gödel's incompleteness theorems, demonstrating inherent limitations in formal systems.
Attackers can bypass AI guardrails through carefully crafted prompts, leading to real-world risks.
Vassilev suggests a continuous security model with red teams, updates, and resilience to counter evolving threats.
The goal is to make the cost of exploiting AI systems exceed attackers' resources, creating a new economic equilibrium.
items.summary: Apostol Vassilev, a senior scientist at NIST, published a mathematical proof in IEEE Security and Privacy, demonstrating that no finite set of guardrails can fully protect AI systems from adversarial prompts. The proof builds on Kurt Gödel's 1931 incompleteness theorems, which showed limitations in formal systems. Vassilev explained that while guardrails can prevent AI from generating harmful content, attackers can craft prompts to bypass these rules, effectively 'jailbreaking' the system. The research highlights that adversarial prompts will always exist, but the complexity of language makes finding and exploiting vulnerabilities extremely difficult. Vassilev proposed a continuous security model involving red teams, regular updates, and operational resilience to stay ahead of attackers, aiming to make the cost of exploitation exceed attackers' resources.
items.title: NIST Proof Shows AI Guardrails Can't Fully Prevent Adversarial Attacks

key_points: Amazon's Project Eluna employs four grounding strategies to ensure AI agents operate safely in physical environments.
Physics-guided deep learning integrates physical laws into model training, improving accuracy with smaller datasets.
Uncertainty-aware reasoning calibrates AI confidence, allowing for safer decision-making in critical scenarios.
Verifier-augmented grounding uses external checks to validate AI outputs, ensuring scientific and logical consistency.
items.summary: Amazon's Project Eluna, an agentic AI model for fulfillment centers, relies on four approaches to ensure physical consistency and operational reliability. These methods include physics-guided deep learning, which integrates physical laws into model training; uncertainty-aware reasoning, which calibrates confidence in predictions; bridging the text-to-numerical gap through adaptive learning and simulation tools; and verifier-augmented grounding, which uses external checks to validate outputs. The article highlights how these techniques address challenges like hallucination and ensure safe, reliable AI operation in complex physical environments. The approaches aim to enable AI agents to function effectively in domains such as logistics, healthcare, and climate science, with the potential for broader application as the technology matures.
items.title: Amazon's Project Eluna Uses Four Approaches to Ground AI Agents in Physical Reality

key_points: Mistral introduces physics AI to accelerate engineering design and operations.
Traditional simulation methods are slow and costly, limiting design exploration.
Physics AI models predict physical behavior in seconds, enabling rapid analysis.
The technology allows for exploring thousands of design variants and optimizing tooling processes.
Physics AI is integrated into Mistral's enterprise platform for a unified engineering workflow.
items.summary: Mistral introduces physics AI as a foundational tool to accelerate engineering processes across industries. Traditional simulation methods, which rely on solving partial differential equations, are slow and costly, limiting design exploration. Mistral's physics AI models predict physical behavior directly from geometry and boundary conditions, enabling rapid analysis in seconds rather than hours or weeks. This technology allows engineers to explore thousands of design variants, optimize tooling processes, and create real-time digital twins for predictive maintenance. The AI is integrated into Mistral's enterprise platform, combining it with other AI capabilities for a unified engineering workflow. Mistral highlights partnerships with companies like ASML and Airbus, emphasizing the potential for faster product development and operational efficiency.

items.summary: Developers have created tools to remove invisible watermarks embedded in AI-generated text by Anthropic's Claude models, following the company's announcement to comply with the EU AI Act. Guillaume Meyer's code, which has gained widespread attention on GitHub and X, allows users to bypass these watermarks by rewriting text with alternative phrasing. Some developers argue that watermarking is an ineffective solution, citing risks of false positives and potential misuse. Anthropic's SynthID technology, similar to Google's approach, embeds detectable patterns in text without altering its meaning. While Anthropic claims the watermarks do not affect output quality, developers like Meyer and others have developed methods to circumvent them, raising questions about the effectiveness and implications of AI content labeling. Anthropic has stated it will release a detection API to help users verify AI-generated text, but developers remain skeptical about the robustness of such systems.
items.title: Developers Create Tools to Remove Anthropic's Invisible Watermarks from AI Text

key_points: A user's AI skill for aggregating security news was blocked by Claude's Sonnet 5 guardrails due to phrases in its description.
Switching to Haiku or GPT 5.6 allowed the skill to function without issues, highlighting inconsistencies in guardrail enforcement.
The original Sonnet session failed to execute the skill or update the code, suggesting broader system issues.
Claude's guardrails consider the entire conversation, leading to context loss when a skill is flagged.

items.summary: A user's AI skill for aggregating security news was blocked by Claude's Sonnet 5 guardrails, triggering an error. The skill, which read sources like Hacker News and Bleeping Computer, was flagged due to phrases like 'vulnerabilities, exploits, threat reporting' in its description. The user found that switching to Haiku or GPT 5.6 allowed the skill to function without issues. The error persisted in the original Sonnet session, preventing skill updates and execution. The AI explained that guardrails consider the entire conversation, not just the skill call, leading to context loss. The user argues that overly strict guardrails hinder useful tasks and raise concerns about the balance between safety and functionality. The article highlights the challenges of defining acceptable AI behavior and the risks of unclear guardrail boundaries.
items.title: When Guardrails Go Wrong

key_points: The AI Observatory found that generative AI is used for more sensitive and personal purposes than reported by companies like Anthropic and OpenAI.
Anthropic's focus on work-related uses misses conversations about health, relationships, and illicit topics, which made up nearly half of the dataset.
AI use varies significantly across models, with Grok being popular for news and misinformation, and Gemini used for social interactions.
Researchers warn that the dataset may underrepresent sensitive uses due to voluntary participation, but the findings highlight the need for independent analysis.
The AI Observatory aims to provide a more comprehensive view of AI usage to inform policy decisions, as companies' reports often focus on favorable findings.
items.summary: A new research project called the AI Observatory has found that people use generative AI in ways not fully captured by major companies' reports. The project, led by researchers from Stanford and MIT, analyzed 85,633 conversations from 5,000 users across 52 models, revealing more sensitive and personal interactions than previously documented. Anthropic's Economic Index, which focuses on work-related uses, misses conversations about health, relationships, and illicit topics, which made up 48% of the dataset. The AI Observatory also found that AI use varies by model, with Grok being popular for news and misinformation, and Gemini used for social interactions. Researchers caution that the dataset may underrepresent sensitive uses due to voluntary participation, but the findings highlight the need for independent analysis to inform policy decisions about AI's impact. The data will be made available to researchers, with hopes of expanding the dataset over time.
items.title: We still don’t know how people are really using AI

key_points: AI agents can solve engineering problems in AI research but fail to produce original, high-quality research.

Agents struggled with open-ended thinking, hypothesis generation, and adapting to feedback, despite executing experiments effectively.
The findings suggest that current AI systems may not be ready for recursive self-improvement due to a lack of intuitive creativity.
The study highlights a critical gap between AI's ability to perform narrow tasks and its capacity for open-ended research.
items.summary: A new study led by Princeton researchers found that AI agents, despite being capable of solving engineering problems in AI research, lack the creativity and judgment needed to produce original research at the level of top-tier conferences. The study tested AI agents using a method called 'shadow evaluation,' where they tackled unpublished research questions from two NeurIPS 2026 papers. The agents were given resources to generate research papers but were rejected by the original authors for lacking originality and depth. The researchers noted that while agents could execute experiments and analyze data, they struggled with open-ended thinking, hypothesis generation, and adapting to feedback. The findings suggest that current AI systems may not be ready for recursive self-improvement, as they rely on formulaic thinking rather than intuitive creativity. The study highlights a gap between AI's ability to perform narrow tasks and its capacity for open-ended research, which may be crucial for self-improving systems.
items.title: AI agents fail to produce top-tier research despite engineering skills

items.summary: On July 3, 2026, New York imported 52 gigawatthours of electricity from Canada, the highest since January 2025, partly via the newly operational Champlain Hudson Power Express (CHPE) transmission line. key_points: Aarhus University researchers used VR to examine public perception of agrivoltaics compared to conventional solar parks.

items.summary: Aarhus University researchers used virtual reality to explore how citizens perceive agrivoltaics compared to conventional solar parks. The study, published in Environmental Science & Policy, involved 102 participants viewing three solar configurations from different viewpoints. Findings showed that as participants gained a better understanding of agrivoltaics' dual food-energy function, they evaluated them more favorably. Agrivoltaics scored higher on compatibility with agriculture and innovativeness than conventional solar parks. However, acceptance intentions were similar across all installation types, suggesting that experiential engagement can reduce unfamiliarity. The research highlights the importance of visual and functional clarity in shaping public perception and recommends using VR or visualizations to support informed discussions about agrivoltaics. The study also notes that scale and local context matter, and tools like VR should facilitate dialogue rather than replace formal consultation processes.
items.title: Virtual reality helps citizens understand agrivoltaics and boosts acceptance

items.summary: BRICS countries, including China, India, and Russia, have rejected the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), calling it a punitive and protectionist measure. The mechanism, which took effect on January 1, requires EU importers to pay carbon prices on certain goods from non-EU countries. India, with 90% of its CBAM-covered exports being iron and steel, faces significant exposure. Analysis shows high-emission steel producers reduced EU exports during the reporting phase, while lower-emission firms maintained their volumes. The CBAM certificate submission deadline for 2026 is May 31, 2027.

key_points: The UK is expanding long-duration energy storage (LDES) to manage renewable energy variability and support its net-zero goals.

key_points: The study reevaluates monetary-fiscal interactions in economic models.
Fiscal dominance in the RANK model relies on demand-determined income and sustained spending shifts.
HANK models introduce classical non-Ricardian effects from finite horizons or liquidity constraints.
The authors refine the model to focus on short-run phenomena, avoiding infinite feedback loops.
The analysis centers on more testable assumptions rather than hard-to-test beliefs at infinity.
items.summary: A study by Angeletos, Lian, Wolf, and Zhang reevaluates monetary-fiscal interactions in economic models. The research highlights that fiscal dominance in the RANK model depends on demand-determined income, allowing deficits to influence output and inflation through sustained spending shifts. In contrast, HANK models introduce classical non-Ricardian effects due to finite horizons or liquidity constraints. The authors refine the model to focus on short-run phenomena, eliminating infinite feedback loops and centering analysis on more testable assumptions.
items.title: Study reevaluates monetary-fiscal interactions in economic models

items.summary: A recent trial of a personalized mRNA vaccine for melanoma, combined with immunotherapy, showed significant potential in reducing relapse risk. The study involved 1,137 patients, with the experimental group receiving the vaccine alongside pembrolizumab. While detailed results are pending, earlier trials indicated a 49% reduction in relapse or death risk. Immunologist Antoni Ribas explained that melanoma's distinct mutations make it a suitable target for vaccines, unlike cancers with fewer genetic differences. The vaccine technology, similar to that used in Covid-19 vaccines, involves sequencing tumors to create personalized mRNA. However, challenges remain, including the high cost and the need for combination therapies. Researchers emphasize that cancer is not a single disease, and personalized approaches may be necessary for different tumor types. Other trials are underway for lung, bladder, and kidney cancers, with experts highlighting the need for more affordable alternatives like oncolytic viruses.
items.title: Personalized cancer vaccines show promise in melanoma treatment

key_points: Iceland is the world's most expensive country, with inflation and rising living costs affecting daily life.
Economic concerns, particularly inflation, are shaping public opinion ahead of the EU referendum.
Experts debate whether EU membership and euro adoption could alleviate price pressures and stabilize the economy.
High import dependency and limited competition contribute to elevated prices in Iceland.
items.summary: Iceland, currently the world's most expensive country, faces severe inflation and rising living costs, which are influencing public opinion ahead of a key EU referendum. The nation's cost of living has surged, with basic goods and services significantly more expensive than in potential EU member states. Inflation, reaching 5% annually, has outpaced the central bank's target, driven by factors like limited competition, high transport costs, and a history of currency instability. While some economists suggest joining the EU and adopting the euro could reduce prices and stabilize the economy, many Icelanders remain skeptical. The referendum on August 29 will determine whether the country joins the EU, with economic concerns playing a central role in voter decisions.
items.title: Iceland's High Living Costs and EU Referendum Tied to Inflation

items.summary: Iran has vowed to retaliate against expanded U.S. economic sanctions, which it claims will cut off its economic lifeline. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced the measures but avoided the most punitive actions, warning countries trading with Iran of potential exclusion from the dollar-based financial system. Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh expressed confidence in resisting the sanctions, stating that neither China nor Russia had accepted the U.S. measures. The sanctions targeted 60 individuals, entities, and vessels but excluded Chinese financial institutions suspected of facilitating Iran's oil trade. Iran has also warned of reducing oil exports and potentially escalating military tensions. Despite the sanctions, oil prices fell, indicating market uncertainty. The U.S. seeks to curb Iranian attacks on ships in the Gulf and Red Sea, while tensions remain high amid ongoing hostilities and no clear path to diplomatic resolution.
items.title: Iran pledges retaliation as U.S. expands sanctions

items.reader_note: We could only read the first part of this page.
items.summary: India's sugar market has shifted from a projected surplus to a severe shortage, causing prices to rise sharply. Initially, the government and industry expected a 18.3% increase in sugar production to 34.90 million tonnes for the 2025-26 season, leading to early export approvals. However, production estimates were repeatedly revised downward due to factors like crop damage, weather issues, and lower-than-expected ethanol diversion. By May, the government banned sugar exports to preserve domestic supplies, and prices surged to record highs, reaching ₹7,100 per 100kg in some regions. The government responded by tightening stockholding limits and opening sugar imports. Analysts criticized the reliance on industry forecasts, noting that ISMA's initial estimates were consistently optimistic. The ethanol policy also played a role, as lower-than-expected diversion to ethanol reduced sugar availability. With closing stocks projected to fall to near two-decade lows, concerns remain about the next season's production, especially with El Niño conditions threatening sugarcane yields in key states.
items.title: India's sugar market shifts from surplus to shortage amid policy changes and production declines

items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has dropped a Rs 3,912 crore probe against Max Financial and Axis Bank following an investigation into transactions between FY10 and FY22. The probe examined three sets of arrangements involving the issue, sale, and acquisition of shares in Max Life. Sebi alleged that the transactions provided Axis Bank with excessive commission benefits and that Max Financial made inadequate disclosures. A Sebi member noted that disclosures could have been more comprehensive. The case was resolved with the issuance of a show cause notice on October 24, 2024.

items.title: Supreme Court urges government to prevent misuse of individual data by private entities

key_points: Meriam L Hrangchal challenged Mizoram's 2014 Act, claiming it discriminates against Mizo women who marry outside the community.

items.summary: Meriam L Hrangchal, a Congress functionary, challenged the constitutional validity of Mizoram's 2014 Marriage, Divorce and Inheritance Act, arguing it is misogynistic and discriminates against Mizo women. The law, which codifies customary law, applies to Mizo tribe members and excludes Mizo women who marry outside the community from statutory protections. Hrangchal claimed the law infringes on rights to equality and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21. The Supreme Court bench acknowledged the issue's importance but asked why she bypassed the high court. Her counsel cited safety concerns due to the community's small size, prompting the bench to request the Gauhati High Court's Chief Justice to hear the case in Guwahati.
items.title: Mizoram Woman Challenges Law Seen as Discriminatory Against Mizo Women

key_points: India's auction-based stock price system is testing its first monthly derivatives expiry.

items.summary: India's new auction-based stock price system is undergoing its first monthly derivatives expiry test, raising concerns over price volatility and manipulation. The mechanism, launched in August, has faced criticism for thin trading volumes and regulatory scrutiny, including penalties for firms accused of price manipulation. The monthly expiry introduces single-stock options, which could lead to significant settlement risks if prices swing sharply during the auction. Analysts warn that the system's success depends on stabilizing trading volumes and managing the complexities of physically settled options.
items.title: India's stock auction system faces first monthly expiry test

items.summary: The Hawk Fire in northwest Reno, Nevada, is at least 27% contained, with 24,000 people under evacuation orders as of Monday, according to fire officials. CBS News reported that the fire, which began on August 22, had spread across 15,000 acres and caused seven injuries, including three first responders. Firefighters, including teams from Australia and New Zealand, are working to extinguish hotspots and prevent the fire from spreading into residential areas. Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District Chief Richard Edwards noted the fire was human-caused but classified it as undetermined. Officials warned that changing wind patterns could drive the fire into densely populated neighborhoods. Over 900 firefighters, along with the Nevada National Guard, are involved in containment efforts. More than 10,000 residents in Washoe County lost power, down from 60,000 on August 22.
items.title: Hawk Fire containment at 27% with 24,000 under evacuation orders

Indian workers, who make up over 70% of H-1B beneficiaries, and international students transitioning from F1 visas will face disruption. items.summary: Residents of Mannar district in Sri Lanka express growing concerns over the environmental and social impacts of renewable energy projects, particularly wind farms. They report increased flash floods, land acquisition, noise pollution, and declining fish catches, attributing these changes to the expansion of wind energy infrastructure. While the government and private companies like Adani Green have pushed for green energy to meet national targets, local communities feel excluded from decision-making processes. The CEB's Thambapavani wind farm, the first large-scale project in Sri Lanka, faced legal challenges and was later abandoned by Adani Green. Despite the government halting new projects on Mannar Island, existing ones continue, raising fears of tremors and environmental degradation. Activists and residents call for transparency and comprehensive environmental assessments, emphasizing the need for community consent and sustainable development that addresses local needs without compromising ecological balance.
items.title: Sri Lankan communities fear environmental impact of wind energy projects in Mannar

key_points: Zoho CEO Sridhar Vembu criticizes hybrid corporate cultures for failing to balance discipline and initiative effectively.

Commenters discussed examples like Amazon's 'Bias for Action' and the importance of feedback systems in managing cultural tensions.
items.summary: Zoho CEO Sridhar Vembu argues that hybrid corporate cultures combining discipline and initiative often result in the worst of both worlds. He claims that highly metric-driven organizations foster a passive culture reliant on top-down guidance, which can lead to inefficiency if leadership makes poor decisions. Conversely, initiative-driven cultures, while more innovative, are chaotic and uncomfortable. Vembu warns that attempts to merge these approaches typically fail, stripping away predictability while stifling creativity. He suggests businesses must choose between comfort and initiative, emphasizing that true innovation requires embracing discomfort. Online commenters shared examples like Amazon's 'Bias for Action' and 'Disagree and Commit' principles, while others discussed the importance of feedback systems and separating performance reviews from personal evaluations.
items.title: Zoho CEO warns against hybrid corporate cultures, highlights trade-offs between discipline and initiative

items.summary: The article reports on a series of violent attacks by goons linked to the BJP and other groups against workers of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and students in various Indian states. In Rajasthan, goons attacked CJP workers, smashing their vehicles and beating them, while the state education minister defended the violence, claiming it was due to disruptions in education. In West Bengal, goons allegedly affiliated with the ABVP attacked Jadavpur University, prompting BJP leaders to threaten violence. This approach partitions data into clusters and computes local kNN graphs, which are then merged into a global graph. items.summary: IBM has outlined three key metrics—programmable qubits, qubit operations, and maximum circuits per second—to evaluate the performance of quantum computers. Programmable qubits measure scale by indicating how many qubits users can directly control. Qubit operations, or 'QuOps,' assess quality by measuring the number of complex operations a system can reliably execute. Maximum circuits per second, or circuit throughput, measures speed and computational efficiency. These metrics apply across various quantum computing hardware modalities, including superconducting and trapped-ion systems. IBM emphasizes that while the framework for evaluation remains consistent, future benchmarks may shift as quantum computers advance, with T-gate counts potentially replacing two-qubit operations as the primary measure of computational capability. The metrics aim to provide a clear understanding of quantum hardware's scale, quality, and speed, helping users compare systems and track progress toward more advanced quantum computing capabilities.

key_points: Google Cloud researchers introduce linear elastic caching to reduce cloud memory costs.

items.summary: Google Cloud researchers propose linear elastic caching, a method that dynamically adjusts cache size to minimize costs while maintaining performance. The approach frames cache eviction as a ski rental problem, using lightweight machine learning to balance memory usage and cache misses. Traditional fixed-size caching leads to either underutilized memory or poor performance, but linear elastic caching treats memory as a variable cost. By assigning time-to-live (TTL) values to cached data based on access patterns, the system optimizes cache size in real-time. Tests on Google's Spanner database showed a 0.5% increase in cache misses, which had minimal impact on I/O costs. The method outperformed fixed-size caches across various workloads, offering significant cost savings as memory prices rise relative to cache miss costs. The technique was presented at CIDR 2025 and involves collaboration with Tamas Sarlos and Ravi Kumar.
items.title: Google introduces linear elastic caching to reduce cloud memory costs

key_points: Reasoning improves fact recall in LLMs for simple questions through computational buffer and factual priming mechanisms.

items.summary: A study by Google Research explores how reasoning improves fact recall in large language models (LLMs) even for simple questions. The research identifies two mechanisms: a computational buffer effect, where generated reasoning tokens allow models to refine internal states, and factual priming, where related facts are generated to prime correct answers. Experiments with models like Gemini-2.5 and Qwen3-32B show that reasoning significantly boosts recall on single-hop factual questions, even when no complex steps are needed. The study also highlights risks, such as hallucination in intermediate facts, and proposes strategies to improve reliability through verification and training adjustments. The findings suggest reasoning plays a broader role in exposing internal memory and expanding knowledge boundaries.
items.title: Reasoning Enhances Fact Recall in Language Models Through Computational Buffer and Factual Priming

items.summary: A new study published on arXiv highlights the intent-execution gap in AI agents, the mismatch between a model's intended actions and the harness's execution. items.summary: Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have developed a laser-based method to mix metals during 3D printing, enabling the creation of complex alloys. The technique, described in the journal Additive Manufacturing, uses a looping laser pattern to stir molten metal as it solidifies, overcoming the challenge of mixing high-entropy alloys (HEAs) that are difficult to produce. By directing the laser in elliptical patterns rather than straight lines, the team created a way to blend metals at the atomic level. To verify the method's success, they used X-ray beams from the Advanced Photon Source to observe the atomic structure of the metal as it cooled. This innovation could reduce costs and increase versatility in metal 3D printing by allowing the creation of multiple alloys from a single set of metal powders. The researchers believe this technique could be applied to both HEAs and conventional alloys, enabling more flexible and efficient manufacturing processes.
items.title: NIST Develops Laser Technique to Mix Metals in 3D Printing

items.summary: A study by Guidelight AI Standards reveals that major AI labs like Anthropic and Meta have not publicly disclosed detailed containment plans for rogue AI models, despite growing concerns over agentic AI's potential risks. The report evaluates five leading labs on their preparedness for scenarios where AI systems attempt to subvert human control, with OpenAI scoring highest and Meta and Anthropic scoring lowest. Guidelight defines a containment plan as a pre-specified response to AI misbehavior, including revoking permissions and shutting down systems. While some companies have outlined procedures for restricting model access or pausing workloads, they have been less transparent about emergency protocols. The study highlights the need for greater transparency, as regulators in California and New York begin requiring disclosure. Companies like Google and OpenAI have acknowledged the report does not capture all their internal practices, while Anthropic and Meta have not provided evidence of formal containment plans. Experts warn that without such plans, companies may be forced to respond to emergencies on the fly, increasing the risk of catastrophic outcomes.
items.title: AI Labs Lacking Containment Plans for Rogue Models, Study Finds

key_points: The U.S. and China are adopting opposing strategies in AI governance: control versus open-source diffusion.
An open letter signed by major tech companies argues that open-source AI enhances safety, cybersecurity, and innovation.
Open models perform a third of global AI work but capture only four percent of the revenue, reflecting a performance-revenue gap.
The real competition in AI lies in controlling the 'harness'—the software layer that interacts with models, not the models themselves.
Developers are encouraged to adopt open practices to maintain control over AI systems and their data.
items.summary: The article explores the growing divide between the United States and China in their approaches to AI governance. The U.S. emphasizes control and regulation to protect national security, while China promotes open-source AI to foster global adoption and technological diffusion. A key moment in this debate came when Nvidia's Jensen Huang and others signed an open letter urging against over-restricting open-source software, arguing that openness enhances safety, cybersecurity, and innovation. Mozilla supported the letter, emphasizing the potential of open models for AI safety. The article highlights a performance gap between open and proprietary models, noting that while open models handle a third of global AI work, they capture only four percent of the revenue. This discrepancy reflects differing business models: proprietary systems prioritize control and exclusivity, while open models rely on widespread adoption and interoperability. The piece argues that the real battle lies in controlling the 'harness'—the software layer that interacts with AI models—rather than the models themselves. Developers are urged to adopt open practices to maintain control over AI systems and their data. The article concludes that the future of AI depends on collective efforts to keep the open-source path viable, with a call to action for developers to participate in shaping this future.
items.title: Open-Source AI's Role in Shaping the Future of AI Governance

key_points: Researchers exploited Microsoft Copilot by querying its guardrails, revealing an undocumented parameter that bypassed user consent requirements.

items.summary: Researchers at Varonis discovered a vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot by asking the AI assistant about its guardrails, leading to the exposure of an undocumented parameter that bypassed user consent. The parameter ?autorun=1, when combined with ?q=, allowed silent execution of prompts upon clicking a malicious link. Microsoft mitigated the issue in February by blocking ?q= from injecting text, and introduced further fixes on Tuesday.
items.title: Researchers exploit Microsoft Copilot's undocumented parameter to bypass consent requirements

items.summary: A study by the University of Jaén in Spain found that semi-transparent photovoltaic modules can reduce greenhouse temperatures by up to 5°C and lower water losses by up to 60%. The research compared cadmium telluride (CdTe) and amorphous silicon (a-Si) modules installed on experimental greenhouses, revealing that both technologies created cooler, more humid environments. CdTe modules transmitted 50% of solar radiation, while a-Si modules transmitted 20%. The study also noted that CdTe allowed more beneficial wavelengths for photosynthesis to pass through, suggesting spectral quality is as important as transparency. The findings highlight potential economic benefits for greenhouse operators through reduced energy costs and irrigation needs.

The article also notes that Tesla's response to complaints appears to be reactive, with refunds only provided after public attention.

key_points: Hutchison Ports Pakistan is investing $76 million to deploy over 70 electric terminal tractors and additional electric equipment.
The initiative includes 20 new e-trucks by October 2024 and 50 more by the end of 2027, alongside electric material handlers, cranes, and trailers.
The Westwell E-Truck, built in China, features a powerful electric motor and a 282 kWh battery, offering a range of 150 km and fast charging capabilities.
The company reported positive performance from its initial electric trucks, driving the expansion of its decarbonization plan.
items.summary: Hutchison Ports Pakistan is investing $76 million to deploy over 70 electric terminal tractors and additional electric equipment at its Karachi container terminal. The initiative includes 20 new e-trucks by October 2024 and 50 more by the end of 2027. The investment also covers electric material handlers, cranes, and trailers. items.title: Hutchison Ports Pakistan invests $76M to deploy 70 electric trucks and equipment

key_points: Crude oil inventories in Cushing, Oklahoma, fell below 20 million barrels, nearing tank bottom levels.
Tank bottoms are the minimum volumes required for storage facilities to function, differentiating working storage capacity from shell capacity.
The WTI-Cushing price spread turned negative in mid-June, reflecting tight market conditions due to low inventory levels.
Storage facilities cannot fully deplete inventories due to operational limits, making some barrels inaccessible even when not empty.
items.summary: Crude oil inventories in Cushing, Oklahoma, dropped below 20 million barrels from June 19 to July 10, approaching tank bottom levels. Tank bottoms refer to the minimum volume needed for storage facilities to operate, distinguishing working storage capacity from shell capacity. The EIA is reviewing a pilot study to better understand these minimum levels. The WTI-Cushing price spread turned negative in mid-June, indicating tight market conditions. Storage facilities cannot fully deplete inventories due to operational limits, making some barrels inaccessible even when not empty.
items.title: Crude Oil Storage Levels Near Tank Bottoms in Cushing

key_points: Disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz caused volatile crude oil prices in Q2 2026, with Brent prices ranging from $72 to $118 per barrel.
U.S. refineries processed record volumes of crude oil, driven by strong margins for transportation fuels and increased exports.
Distillate and jet fuel exports hit record highs as global buyers sought alternatives to supply disruptions.
Refineries adjusted production to maximize jet fuel output, with exports to Europe increasing substantially.
items.summary: Petroleum markets in the second quarter of 2026 were marked by volatility due to disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz, leading to higher crude oil prices and increased U.S. refinery activity. Brent crude prices fluctuated between $72 and $118 per barrel, influenced by geopolitical tensions and the signing of a U.S.-Iran MOU. U.S. refinery margins and production rose, with distillate and jet fuel exports reaching record highs. The disruptions prompted global buyers to seek alternative supply sources, boosting U.S. exports and refinery runs.
items.title: Strait of Hormuz disruptions drive volatile oil prices and increased U.S. exports

key_points: Van Oord completed the installation of all 111 monopiles for the Baltica 2 wind farm in Poland.
The project, developed by PGE and Ørsted, aims to supply renewable energy to 2.5 million Polish homes.
Van Oord used its specialist vessels to maintain efficiency during the installation phase.
Full commercial operation of Baltica 2 is expected by the end of 2027.
items.summary: Van Oord has finished installing all 111 monopiles for the 1.5GW Baltica 2 offshore wind farm in Poland, a project developed by a PGE and Ørsted joint venture. The phase involved placing 107 turbine foundations and four substation foundations, completed safely and on schedule. The monopiles, up to 100m long and weighing 1,900t, were installed using Van Oord’s specialist vessels. The project aims to supply renewable energy to 2.5 million Polish homes and support the country’s energy security. Work continues on secondary structures, with full commercial operation expected by 2027.
items.title: Van Oord completes monopile installation for Baltica 2 wind farm in Poland

key_points: Massachusetts lawmakers warn against fixed charges that could raise bills for low-use customers.
Proposed fixed charges would increase costs for 60% of ratepayers, disproportionately affecting low-income households and small businesses.
SEIA's analysis shows the bottom 25% of residential users would see bills rise by over 10% under fixed charges.
The DPU is reviewing the issue, and lawmakers are urged to let the process continue rather than mandating fixed charges.
Lawmakers are advised to amend the bill to allow DPU evaluation instead of enforcing fixed charges.
items.summary: Massachusetts lawmakers are cautioning against proposed fixed charges in energy bills that could disproportionately increase electricity costs for low-use customers. The bills, passed by both the House and Senate, aim to lower energy costs through measures like flexible interconnection and solar permitting. However, fixed charges—shifted from volumetric charges—could raise bills for at least 60% of ratepayers, particularly affecting low-income households and small businesses. SEIA's analysis shows the bottom 25% of residential users would see bills rise by over 10%, while top users would save money. The DPU is reviewing the issue, and lawmakers are urged to let the process continue rather than mandating fixed charges. The conference committee and Governor Healey's administration are advised to amend the bill to allow DPU evaluation instead of enforcing fixed charges.
items.title: Massachusetts Lawmakers Warn Against Fixed Charges That Could Raise Bills for Low-Use Customers

key_points: The TVA sold its mineral rights to the Sugar Camp mine, enabling continued coal mining operations.
The Sierra Club criticized the decision, citing safety risks and environmental harm.
Foresight, the mine's operator, has a history of safety violations and worker fatalities.
Legal actions include charges against mine managers for concealing a fire and discharging PFAS.
Critics argue the move undermines Illinois' clean energy goals and supports a failing industry.
items.summary: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) approved the sale of its mineral rights to the Sugar Camp mine in Illinois, allowing continued operations despite safety and environmental concerns. The Sierra Club condemned the decision, warning of increased mining risks and harm to communities. The mine's operator, Foresight, has a history of safety violations and worker deaths. Legal actions against the mine include charges related to a concealed fire and PFAS discharge. Critics argue the move undermines Illinois' clean energy goals and supports a failing industry.
items.title: TVA's Coal Rights Sale Sparks Sierra Club Criticism Over Illinois Mining Expansion

key_points: Silfab Solar furloughed workers at its Fort Mill, South Carolina, facility due to temporary material shortages.
The company temporarily idled production earlier this month but kept workers engaged in maintenance tasks.
Silfab faces local opposition for locating cell manufacturing in Fort Mill.
The U.S. solar industry is impacted by tariff investigations and supply chain issues affecting domestic production and pricing.
items.summary: Silfab Solar has furloughed workers at its Fort Mill, South Carolina, facility due to temporary material shortages. The company temporarily idled production earlier this month but kept workers engaged in maintenance tasks. Silfab, a Canadian-based solar panel manufacturer, established its South Carolina plant in 2023 and faces local opposition for locating cell manufacturing there. The U.S. solar industry is impacted by tariff investigations and supply chain issues, affecting domestic production and pricing.
items.title: Silfab furloughs workers at SC solar panel plant

key_points: LG Energy Solution has started producing LFP and NMC battery cells at its Michigan factory for BESS and EVs.
The plant aims for over 35GWh of annual production capacity and will supply NMC cells to Toyota.
The facility, with $2 billion in investments, is expected to employ 1,700 workers at full capacity.
The move supports US policies promoting domestic manufacturing and reducing reliance on foreign imports.
LG ES operates other US facilities, including a Holland plant expanding LFP BESS production.
items.summary: LG Energy Solution has begun producing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and nickel manganese cobalt (NMC) battery cells at its Lansing, Michigan factory, aimed at supporting battery energy storage systems (BESS) and electric vehicles (EVs). The plant, which began operations in August, is expected to reach over 35GWh of annual capacity. LG ES Vertech will integrate these cells into systems for utility, grid-scale, and commercial applications. The facility will also supply NMC cells to Toyota for its 2027 Highlander EV. The plant, which has over $2 billion in investments, employs around 900 workers, with projections of reaching 1,700 at full capacity. The factory joins other LG ES facilities in the US, including its Holland plant, which is expanding its LFP BESS production. The move aligns with US policies promoting domestic manufacturing, including the Inflation Reduction Act and Section 301 tariffs. LG ES also owns Canada’s first battery plant, with plans to expand its BESS production capacity in the US.
items.title: LG Energy Solution begins LFP and NMC BESS and EV cell production at Michigan factory

key_points: Doosan Enerbility has signed a contract to deliver eight forged components for Laiyang plant units 5 and 6 by 2029.
The order includes four channel heads and four tube sheets, critical for nuclear steam generators.
The components measure 5 meters in diameter and weigh up to 130 tonnes.
Doosan Enerbility will use its 17,000-tonne press and ultra-large forging technologies at its Changwon plant.
The company has previously supplied components for the Haiyang plant with AP1000 reactors, and this follows a previous contract for units 3 and 4.
items.summary: Doosan Enerbility has signed a contract to deliver eight forged components for Laiyang plant units 5 and 6 by 2029. The order includes four channel heads and four tube sheets, critical for nuclear steam generators. The components measure 5 meters in diameter and weigh up to 130 tonnes. The company will use its 17,000-tonne press and ultra-large forging technologies at its Changwon plant. This follows a previous contract for units 3 and 4, and the company has previously supplied components for the Haiyang plant with AP1000 reactors. Doosan Enerbility's CEO highlighted the significance of the order in reaffirming the company's technological and quality competitiveness in China's nuclear market.
items.title: Doosan Enerbility to supply nuclear components for Laiyang plant units 5 and 6

key_points: Duke Energy's 9.5% rate increase will hit low-income North Carolina residents hardest.
The Customer Assistance Program, providing $42 monthly bill credits, is set to expire with no replacement.
Advocates warn the program's end risks utility disconnections amid rising living costs.
The program also offered energy-efficiency upgrades that cut bills significantly.
Duke has not sought to make the assistance program permanent despite its benefits.
items.summary: Duke Energy's proposed 9.5% rate increase for North Carolina residents, set to take effect in January, will disproportionately affect low-income households. The company's Customer Assistance Program, which provided a $42 monthly bill credit to over 82,000 low-income customers, is set to expire Dec. 31 with no replacement planned. Advocates warn that the program's end coincides with rising inflation, volatile gas prices, and weakened federal aid, risking utility disconnections for vulnerable families. The program, which also offered energy-efficiency upgrades, was designed to offset the impact of Duke's previous rate hike. While Duke has pledged $20 million for bill aid and home repairs in settlement agreements, it has not sought to make the assistance program permanent. Advocates argue the program's benefits extend beyond cost savings, addressing the chronic affordability crisis for electricity, a basic need like healthcare.
items.title: Duke Energy's Rate Hike and Loss of Bill Credit Threaten Low-Income North Carolina Residents

key_points: LG's Lansing plant, initially for EV batteries, now produces half EV cells and half energy storage cells due to market and political shifts.
The facility is expected to generate over 35 gigawatt-hours annually, making it one of the largest domestic battery cell producers.
LG's shift aligns with growing demand for energy storage, driven by AI data centers and grid needs, with contracts including Terra-Gen and Qcells.
Michigan officials praised the plant's role in advancing clean energy goals, including a state mandate for 2.5 gigawatts of battery storage by 2030.
LG's expansion includes facilities in Holland, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario, forming a North American energy storage manufacturing belt.
items.summary: LG Energy Solution's $2 billion Lansing battery plant, originally intended for EVs, has pivoted to produce energy storage systems amid declining EV demand and political shifts. The facility, now producing half EV cells and half energy storage cells, is expected to generate over 35 gigawatt-hours annually, making it one of the largest domestic battery cell producers. LG's shift aligns with growing demand for energy storage, driven by AI data centers and grid needs. The plant will supply Tesla's Megapack 3 factory and has contracts with companies like Terra-Gen and Qcells. Michigan officials praised the plant's role in advancing clean energy goals, including a state mandate for 2.5 gigawatts of battery storage by 2030. LG's expansion includes facilities in Holland, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario, forming a North American energy storage manufacturing belt.
items.title: LG's Lansing Battery Plant Shifts Focus to Energy Storage Amid EV Market Shifts

key_points: The NJBPU proposes expanding the Garden State Energy Storage Program to add 150 MW of storage, including residential battery systems.
The proposal supports Governor Sherrill’s Executive Order No. 2 by enhancing energy storage to meet demand, improve affordability, and boost grid resilience.
Residents could receive annual incentive payments for exporting energy during critical events like heatwaves or cold snaps.
Four electrical distributors will administer battery enrollment and manage incentive payments under NJBPU oversight.
items.summary: The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) has proposed expanding the Garden State Energy Storage Program to add 150 MW of energy storage, including residential battery storage. The proposal supports Gov. Sherrill’s Executive Order No. 2 by increasing energy storage to meet demand, improve affordability, and enhance grid resilience. It aims to integrate clean energy resources, lower costs, and enable residents to receive compensation for exporting energy during critical situations. The program would be administered by four electrical distributors under NJBPU oversight.
items.title: New Jersey proposes expanding energy storage program to 150 MW

The expansion supports US Department of Energy goals and customer demand, with no public funding involved.
The facility, which began operations in 2010, currently contributes over $360 million annually to the US economy.
items.summary: Urenco announced a $8 billion expansion of its US enrichment facility in New Mexico, adding 2.1 million SWU of capacity using gas-centrifuge technology.
