Challenges include the rapid pace of technological change and the need for significant investments in monitoring and infrastructure.
items.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has launched the IT Resilience Index (ITRI), a quantitative tool to assess the robustness of technology systems in market infrastructure institutions (MIIs). The index aims to evaluate the ability of MIIs, such as stock exchanges and clearing corporations, to handle operational shocks, cyber threats, and technical failures. SEBI's ITRI is based on nine weighted parameters, with availability and security given the highest priority. The initiative reflects a shift from compliance-based oversight to risk-monitoring frameworks, aligning with global trends in operational resilience. However, challenges remain, including the rapid pace of technological change and the need for substantial investments in automated monitoring systems. SEBI's ITRI could serve as a global model for future-ready financial architecture if implemented effectively.
items.title: SEBI Introduces ITRI to Measure Financial Market Technology Resilience

key_points: Wolf attacks on livestock in Mahuadanr Sanctuary peak at night and early morning, during winter and early summer, and near forest edges.
Over half of surveyed households reported livestock losses, with 415 goats killed and an estimated economic loss of ₹21 lakhs.

Tribal communities tolerate wolves despite livestock losses, viewing them as part of the natural landscape.
The study recommends predator-proof enclosures, improved livestock management, and protecting denning habitats to reduce conflict.
items.summary: A study from India's first wolf sanctuary, Mahuadanr in Jharkhand, found that wolf attacks on livestock are most likely at night and early morning, during winter and early summer, and near forest edges. Over half of surveyed households reported livestock losses, with 415 goats killed and an estimated economic loss of ₹21 lakhs. Researchers identified ecological and socio-economic factors influencing attacks, noting that proximity to the sanctuary boundary increased losses. Despite significant livestock depredation, many tribal communities tolerate wolves, viewing them as part of the natural landscape. The study recommends targeted mitigation strategies, including predator-proof enclosures and improved livestock management, to reduce conflict while supporting conservation efforts.
items.title: Study from India’s first wolf sanctuary reveals when livestock are most at risk

key_points: A man accused of harassment and blackmailing a family whose three members died in the Godavari River has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh.
The family members, including an engineer and his wife, died near the Road-cum-Rail Bridge in Rajamahendravaram, with their 10-year-old grandson rescued.
Police allege the accused threatened and blackmailed the family using private videos, with a suicide note accusing him of poisoning the husband and staging his death as a suicide.
Six teams have been formed to investigate the case, including examining the suicide notes and the circumstances of the family's deaths.
A former MP has called for a CBI or NIA probe, alleging a wider conspiracy and international links.
items.summary: A man accused of harassing and blackmailing a family whose three members died after jumping into the Godavari River in Andhra Pradesh has been arrested in Uttar Pradesh. Shaik Sadiq Khan, the accused, was arrested in Meerut on August 22 following a multi-state search. The family members, including an engineer and his wife, died near the Road-cum-Rail Bridge in Rajamahendravaram. Their 10-year-old grandson was rescued. Police allege Khan harassed the family, threatened them, and blackmailed them using private videos. A suicide note from the daughter accused Khan of poisoning her husband and making his death appear a suicide. Khan is also linked to a separate murder case. Authorities have formed six teams to investigate the case, which includes examining the suicide notes and the circumstances surrounding the family's deaths. A former MP has called for a CBI or NIA probe, alleging a wider conspiracy and international links.
items.title: Engineer's family dies in Godavari; suspect arrested in UP

key_points: The Allahabad High Court rejected a student's claim that wearing a headscarf is an essential religious practice for constitutional protection.
The court stated that the petition lacked the necessary factual and legal foundation to support the assertion.
The school's uniform policy was upheld as a legitimate institutional rule, not discriminatory.
Muslim clerics criticized the ruling, arguing that hijab is an integral part of Islam and should be allowed within school dress codes.
The case underscores the court's requirement for clear evidence to establish religious practices as essential for constitutional claims.
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court dismissed a petition from a student who sought to continue wearing a headscarf with her school uniform in Class 11. The student had worn the scarf since Class 6 without prior objection, but the school refused admission, citing its dress code. The court ruled that the claim of the headscarf being an essential religious practice was a 'bare assertion' lacking necessary factual and legal foundation. It emphasized that schools have the authority to enforce uniform policies as part of their disciplinary framework, provided they are applied without discrimination. The judgment drew criticism from Muslim clerics, who argued that hijab is an integral part of Islam and should be permitted within school dress codes. The court's decision highlights the distinction between institutional rules and constitutional claims, rejecting the petition on the grounds that it failed to meet the required legal standards.
items.title: Allahabad High Court Rules Headscarf Not Essential Religious Practice for Constitutional Claim

key_points: Israeli strikes at Nasser Hospital in Gaza killed 22 people, including journalists, with no accountability sought one year later.
An anonymous Israeli soldier claims the military found no evidence linking the targeted camera to Hamas, contradicting official statements.
The Israeli military has not provided details about its investigation or a timeline, despite repeated requests from The Associated Press.
Rights groups and journalists criticize Israel’s pattern of retroactive incrimination of Palestinians, raising concerns about transparency and accountability.
The strikes, involving four tank shell attacks, have raised questions about the military’s rationale and potential war crimes, including accusations of a 'double tap' attack on first responders.
items.summary: One year after Israeli strikes killed 22 people, including journalists, at Nasser Hospital in Gaza, no one has been held accountable. The attacks, which occurred on August 25, 2025, targeted a suspected Hamas camera on the hospital roof, but subsequent investigations have failed to confirm militant links among the victims. An anonymous Israeli soldier reported that the military found no evidence connecting the camera, belonging to Reuters cameraman Hussam al-Masri, to Hamas. The soldier also claimed none of the six individuals identified as Hamas-linked were the intended targets. The Israeli military has not provided details about its investigation or a timeline for completion, despite repeated requests from The Associated Press. Rights groups and journalists have criticized Israel’s lack of accountability, noting a pattern of retroactive incrimination of Palestinians. The strikes, which involved four tank shell attacks, resulted in the deaths of 33-year-old AP journalist Mariam Dagga and others, raising questions about the military’s rationale and potential war crimes. AP and Reuters have called for transparency and access to Gaza for journalists covering the conflict.
items.title: Israeli strikes at Gaza hospital killed journalists; accountability remains elusive

items.summary: iranian security forces used mosques across tehran as bases to monitor and confront protesters during a deadly crackdown in january, according to evidence obtained by iran international. intercepted communications, video footage, and eyewitness accounts show security personnel operating from several mosques, including imam hossein mosque, to deploy forces and equipment. witnesses described security activity around mosques after electricity was cut, with drones flying overhead. the report suggests some mosques functioned as operational bases rather than just places of worship. the crackdown occurred amid widespread protests in iran, which have since been overshadowed by the broader conflict involving iran, israel, and the united states. washington has shifted toward economic pressure, with new sanctions against iran-linked entities and warnings to countries doing business with tehran. iran's rial has fallen to a record low, adding to economic strain, while pakistan has sent a delegation to encourage negotiations between washington and tehran.

items.summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian firms for facilitating the import of Iranian petrochemical products, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at cutting Iran's financial lifelines. key_points: The Supreme Court will form a special bench to assess the application of its March 11 OBC creamy-layer judgment to the 2025 civil services exam.

The Department of Personnel and Training seeks permission to allocate services to 958 candidates under the previous creamy-layer rules.
The government contends that candidates who applied under the old administrative interpretation may have acted on the legal position in force at the time.
The court will consider setting up a special bench to address these concerns, with the government seeking clarity on the judgment's application to the completed process.
items.summary: The Supreme Court has agreed to form a special bench to examine whether its March 11 judgment on OBC creamy-layer criteria applies to the 2025 civil services exam. The Centre argues that applying the ruling to the completed selection process could lead to unequal treatment of candidates and delay training and cadre allocation. The Department of Personnel and Training seeks permission to allocate services to 958 candidates recommended under the previous creamy-layer rules. The government contends that candidates who applied under the old administrative interpretation may have acted on the legal position in force at the time, and a retrospective application of the judgment could create disparities. The court will consider setting up a special bench to address these concerns, with the government seeking clarity on the judgment's application to the completed process.
items.title: Supreme Court may form special bench on OBC quota rules for civil services exam

items.summary: Human Rights Watch reports that Colombian drug gangs and rebel groups are recruiting children through social media to pilot explosive drones, marking a shift in their tactics. The report highlights that at least 1,500 children have been recruited since 2021, with 625 cases reported in 2024 alone. Armed groups are using platforms like Meta and TikTok to lure children, with algorithms potentially promoting content that encourages recruitment. HRW verified videos of children operating drones and noted that some commanders presented drone use as a game. The report also found that nearly half of the recruited children are Indigenous, and girls make up 40% of the cases. HRW urges the Colombian government to strengthen protections and hold recruiters accountable, while calling on social media companies to improve reporting tools.
items.title: Colombian drug gangs use social media to recruit children for drone operations

items.summary: The US has sanctioned four Indian companies for importing petroleum and petrochemical products from Iran, according to the State Department. The firms include Portease Partners LLP and its partners, Sadashiva Overseas Limited, PP Softtech Private Limited, and Prakrutees Infra Impex Private Limited. The sanctions, part of Operation Economic Outcast, aim to cut off Iran's financial lifelines by targeting its oil revenue. The companies were listed for knowingly engaging in transactions involving Iranian petroleum products, with Sadashiva Overseas importing $69 million worth of goods. The Treasury Secretary described the campaign as unprecedented, seeking to pressure Iran into changing its policies through economic measures.

key_points: India's DGCA is considering expanding annual random drug tests for all 12,000 commercial pilots, potentially making it the first country with such a policy.

items.summary: India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is considering expanding drug testing for commercial pilots from 10% to 100% annual random testing, potentially making it the first country with such a policy. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu stated that the proposal aims to enhance safety but acknowledges the operational challenges for airlines. The move follows an incident where an Air India pilot tested positive for narcotics, prompting one-time testing of all pilots. Airlines would need to manage increased testing volumes, infrastructure, and crew downtime. While some airlines already conduct higher testing rates, the DGCA is assessing the balance between safety improvements and operational feasibility. The Federation of Indian Pilots supports expanded testing but advocates for a gradual increase and the use of oral-fluid testing alongside urine-based methods.
items.title: India Considers Annual Random Drug Tests for All Airline Pilots

key_points: The ex-mill price of sugar fell 18% to ₹55/kg after government intervention to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding.

Government measures, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices.
Wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg, with gaps of ₹2-3/kg and ₹7-8/kg respectively between ex-mill and these levels.
items.summary: The ex-mill price of sugar dropped 18% to ₹55 per kg following government measures to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding, according to Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra. Prices had previously surged to ₹67/kg due to mills increasing rates, which Chopra attributed to non-fundamental factors. The government's actions, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices. While ex-mill prices are expected to fall further, wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg respectively. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories noted a ₹2-3/kg gap between ex-mill and wholesale prices, and a ₹7-8/kg gap between ex-mill and retail prices.
items.title: Government intervention lowers sugar ex-mill prices to ₹55/kg, curbing speculation and hoarding

They seek an immediate stay on the August 12 notification, warning of economic hardship for thousands of drivers.
The case is scheduled for urgent consideration on August 26.
items.summary: Four app-based cab drivers in Mumbai have filed a petition with the Bombay High Court challenging Maharashtra's new rule requiring Marathi language proficiency for auto-rickshaw, taxi, and app-based drivers. Petitioners claim nearly 9.65 lakh permits and badges have been issued, with many drivers unable to speak Marathi. items.title: Mumbai drivers challenge Marathi language rule in court, citing livelihood risks

items.summary: An exhibition titled 'What Women Carry' explores the personal items women take when leaving home, highlighting their significance in migration and memory. The display includes photographs and handwritten accounts of objects like jewelry, clothing, and heirlooms, connected by red threads to form a narrative of loss and continuity. Organized by the Margins to Access Project, the exhibition features stories of women who fled conflict, violence, or economic hardship, carrying fragments of their past with them. One woman described wearing a necklace as a connection to her homeland, while others carried items with emotional weight, such as a dress from Myanmar or shirts belonging to a deceased husband. The exhibition emphasizes the often-overlooked labor of women in migration, who rebuild domestic life and preserve cultural practices. The organizers argue that displacement is not just about movement but also about carrying memory and maintaining connections to the past.
items.title: Exhibition captures women's personal belongings as symbols of displacement and memory

key_points: A study found that over 70% of ornamental plants sold online in India are alien species, many of which are invasive or naturalised in other countries.
57 invasive species already declared harmful in India are still available for purchase online, highlighting biosecurity gaps.
The online ornamental plant trade increases propagule pressure and geographic spread, bypassing biosecurity checkpoints.
Researchers suggest implementing risk-assessment protocols, public awareness campaigns, and regulatory measures to mitigate invasion risks.
A screening tool based on 'invasive elsewhere' metrics is proposed to prioritise species for further evaluation.
items.summary: A study published in Environmental Conservation reveals that a majority of ornamental plants sold online in India are alien species, many of which are invasive or naturalised in other countries. Researchers analyzed data from three major online retailers and found 1,371 out of 1,856 species were alien, with 327 classified as invasive elsewhere. The study highlights biosecurity gaps, noting that 57 invasive species already declared harmful in India are still available for purchase. Lead author Kesang Bhutia explains that ornamental plants often escape cultivation and naturalise, posing ecological risks. The online trade, facilitated by e-commerce platforms, increases propagule pressure and geographic spread, bypassing biosecurity checkpoints. The authors suggest implementing risk-assessment protocols, public awareness campaigns, and regulatory measures to mitigate invasion risks. They also propose a screening tool based on 'invasive elsewhere' metrics to prioritise species for further evaluation.
items.title: Online ornamental plant trade in India includes many invasive species
